engine_label: Claude (Sonnet) via claude -p, web search on
question: What public data sources show apartment construction permits in Texas?
answer:
## Public data sources for Texas apartment construction permits

**Federal / statewide (free, aggregated)**
- **U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS)** — the primary source. Reports units authorized by permit-issuing places, broken out by structure size (5+ units = apartments), at national/state/metro(CBSA)/county/place level, monthly and annual.
- **Texas Real Estate Research Center (Texas A&M), trerc.tamu.edu** — republishes the Census BPS data (usually within 2 days of the official release) with a friendlier interface, including an "advanced search by place" tool and MSA-level housing reports. Good if you want Texas-specific permit trends without wrangling raw Census files.
- **HUD's State of the Cities Data Systems (SOCDS) Building Permits Database** — another Census BPS-derived tool with historical place-level permit data, useful for time series by city.
- **FRED (St. Louis Fed)** — has pre-built Census BPS series for Texas, e.g. permits for structures with 5+ units, if you just want a chart/CSV without querying Census directly.

**City/county open data portals (raw permit-level records, often with address, unit count, valuation, status)**
- **Austin**: data.austintexas.gov — has dedicated datasets like "Issued Construction Permits" and "Currently Active Commercial Multifamily Construction Permits."
- **Dallas**: dallasopendata.com — "Building Permits" dataset (OData API available).
- **San Antonio**: data.sanantonio.gov, maintained by the Development Services Department.
- **Houston**: no full open-data permit portal comparable to the above; permit lookups go through the Houston Permitting Center (iPermits) and the Housing and Community Development Department's Housing Resource & Data Center, so coverage/structure differs from Austin/Dallas/San Antonio.
- **Fort Worth, El Paso, and other cities**: check each municipality's permitting department or open-data site individually — coverage is uneven statewide.

**Private/commercial aggregators (paid, more polished, often forward-looking pipeline data)**
- **Zonda** (formerly Metrostudy) — construction/permit tracking widely used by homebuilders and multifamily developers.
- **Yardi Matrix** — apartment-specific construction pipeline and permit-to-delivery tracking.
- **CoStar** — commercial/multifamily permits and construction pipeline as part of its CRE data platform.
- **RealPage** — apartment market and supply-pipeline data.
- **Dodge Construction Network (Dodge Data & Analytics)** — construction starts/permits data across sectors.
- Smaller scrape-based tools like **PermitVector**, **BuildChek**, and **PermitTap** aggregate several Texas city portals into one searchable feed, though coverage of Houston in particular tends to be thinner.

For most research purposes, start with Census BPS via the **Texas Real Estate Research Center** for state/metro trend data, then drop into the individual **city open data portals** (Austin, Dallas, San Antonio) for permit-level detail; Houston requires going through its own permitting/housing department resources since it lacks an equivalent open dataset.

Sources:
- [Building Permits | Texas Real Estate Research Center](https://trerc.tamu.edu/data/building-permits/)
- [Building Permit Place Advanced Search | Texas Real Estate Research Center](https://trerc.tamu.edu/data/building-permit-place-advanced-search/)
- [Building Permits Survey (BPS) — U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/construction/bps/index.html)
- [Housing Resource & Data Center — City of Houston](https://houstontx.gov/housing/research.html)
- [Currently Active Commercial Multifamily Construction Permits | City of Austin](https://data.austintexas.gov/Building-and-Development/Currently-Active-Commercial-Multifamily-Constructi/hah9-7x5p)
- [Issued Construction Permits | City of Austin](https://data.austintexas.gov/Building-and-Development/Issued-Construction-Permits/3syk-w9eu)
- [Building Permits — Dallas OpenData](https://www.dallasopendata.com/Services/Building-Permits/e7gq-4sah)
- [Building Permits — Open Data SA, City of San Antonio](https://data.sanantonio.gov/dataset/building-permits)
